# Billing System Migration Rollout Plan
## 40,000 Users — Old and New Systems Running in Parallel

## Overview

This plan migrates 40,000 users from the legacy billing system to the new billing system in three phases, using dual-running (parallel) operation to allow safe validation and rollback at each stage. The old system remains fully active and untouched through all user-migration phases; its retirement is handled as a separate, later phase after the final batch of users has been migrated and validated.

---

## Phase 1: Canary (5% — 2,000 users)

**Entry criterion:** New billing system has passed end-to-end integration testing in staging, including invoice generation, payment capture, tax calculation, and dunning/retry logic; reconciliation job between old and new systems is deployed and verified against synthetic test accounts; rollback procedure has been tested at least once in staging.

**Population:** Internal employee accounts and opted-in low-risk external users (no active disputes, no complex proration/credits, single-currency billing).

**Duration:** Minimum 10 business days, spanning at least one full billing cycle for the included users.

**Activities:** Route selected accounts' billing events to the new system while keeping the old system's records as the system of record for support/reporting. Run automated daily reconciliation comparing invoice totals, payment status, and tax line items between both systems. Manual finance review of every discrepancy.

---

## Phase 2: Expansion (30% — 12,000 users)

**Entry criterion:** Phase 1 completed its full duration with zero unresolved critical discrepancies; reconciliation mismatch rate stayed below the halt threshold defined below for 5 consecutive business days; support ticket volume attributable to billing errors did not exceed 2x the pre-migration baseline; sign-off from Finance and Support leads.

**Population:** Broader mix of subscription tiers and geographies, still excluding highest-value enterprise accounts and known edge cases (multi-entity billing, custom contracts, heavy proration histories).

**Duration:** Minimum 14 business days, covering at least one full billing cycle.

**Activities:** Continue dual-write/reconciliation. Introduce customer-facing communication (email notice of billing system update) to a subset to validate messaging and support load. Expand automated alerting to cover payment gateway error rates and webhook delivery success by cohort.

---

## Phase 3: General Availability (65% — 26,000 remaining users)

**Entry criterion:** Phase 2 completed its full duration with reconciliation mismatch rate and payment failure delta both within threshold for the entire period; no Sev1/Sev2 billing incidents open; customer support queue for billing issues has returned to within 1.5x of pre-migration baseline; capacity/load testing confirms the new system can handle 100% of transaction volume with headroom.

**Population:** All remaining users, including enterprise and edge-case accounts, migrated in scheduled sub-batches (e.g., by billing date or account tier) to spread load and support demand rather than a single simultaneous cutover.

**Duration:** Minimum 21 business days to allow every migrated user to complete at least one full billing cycle on the new system before the phase is considered closed.

**Activities:** Complete migration of all remaining accounts. Maintain full dual-running reconciliation through the entire phase. Old system continues operating as a live fallback and audit reference; no decommissioning, disabling, or data deletion occurs during this phase.

---

## Phase 4 (Post-Migration): Legacy Decommissioning

Explicitly separated from Phase 3. **Entry criterion:** All 40,000 users have completed at least one full billing cycle on the new system with clean reconciliation; a defined data-retention period (e.g., 90 days) has elapsed on the old system for audit purposes; finance/compliance sign-off obtained. Only after this phase begins may the old system be moved to read-only, then disabled, then decommissioned — as its own sequenced sub-steps, not bundled together.

---

## Halt Metric

**Automated rollout halt trigger:** If the daily reconciliation mismatch rate (invoice or payment records disagreeing between old and new systems) exceeds **0.5% of migrated accounts** on any given day, or if payment failure rate for migrated users exceeds **1.5x** the trailing 30-day baseline failure rate for the old system, the current phase is immediately frozen — no further accounts are migrated — pending root-cause investigation and Finance/Engineering sign-off to resume.

---

## Risks

RISK: Dual-write logic causes duplicate or missed charges during reconciliation window | Implement idempotency keys on all payment operations and run automated daily reconciliation with alerting on any mismatch | Engineering Lead
RISK: Enterprise accounts with custom contracts or proration rules break in the new system | Exclude complex accounts from Phases 1–2, build dedicated test cases from real contract data, and migrate them only in scheduled Phase 3 sub-batches with extra manual QA | Billing Platform Owner
RISK: Customer confusion or distrust from unexpected billing changes or duplicate charges | Proactive customer communication before each user's migration, dedicated support runbook, and temporary fee-credit policy for confirmed billing errors | Customer Support Lead
RISK: Old system is decommissioned before all migrated data is fully validated, causing irreversible data loss | Enforce a mandatory Phase 4 gate with a minimum retention period and explicit sign-off before any disabling or deletion of the old system | VP of Engineering
RISK: New system cannot handle full transaction volume at 100% cutover, causing payment processing delays | Run load/capacity testing against projected Phase 3 volume before phase entry and keep old system warm as an active fallback | Site Reliability Engineering Lead

PHASES: 3
